//: The measured cell and pinned font for this machine, and the design system's own self-contradictions. A contradiction is a bug in .claude/design/, removed when the design is fixed upstream — never when the app changes. See crates/review/src/baseline.rs.

contradictions.design_says: HANDOFF.md:232-241 closes the glyph table at `▌ ● ◐ ○ ✔ ▶ █ + -`, and IMPORT.md restates it as closed.
contradictions.design_also_says: The same document mandates `·` as the top bar's within-group separator (:142, :254-255), `→` on first run's `more` row (:336), `⏎` and `↑↓` in two footers (:280, :341), and presupposes `…` for clipping.
contradictions.app_follows: The copy. A frame cannot draw the screens the design specifies without these five marks, so the table is the half that is wrong.

contradictions.design_says: HANDOFF.md:232-241's closed glyph table contains no box-drawing characters, and Turn 13's rule is that nothing inside a frame is stroked.
contradictions.design_also_says: The design system has no table component at all, and a one-dimensional ground ladder cannot express a two-dimensional grid of cell boundaries.
contradictions.app_follows: ADR 0002 — a markdown table in assistant prose is drawn with `┌ ┬ ┐ ├ ┼ ┤ └ ┴ ┘ ─ │`, scoped to that one construct. This entry is retired when the design system gains a table component.

contradictions.design_says: HANDOFF.md:275 — the permission panel's command block is 'a recessed field on --t-recess'; HANDOFF.md:277 — between the key/value table and the options, 'One row of the recessed tone, blank row'.
contradictions.design_also_says:
5a's own rendered frame uses --t-recess nowhere. The command field is --t-ground, and between the last fact row and the first option there is a single
and nothing else. Measured off `Agent TUI v2.dc.html`, 2026-09-19; the measurement is restated at crates/tui/src/ui/decision.rs:545-553.
contradictions.app_follows: The frame, per CLAUDE.md's first design rule — measure the handoff HTML; reading it is not enough. Two independent stage 5 judges raised both halves as the top findings of the same run, which is what this entry exists to stop the next one doing. Note the light-theme consequence is real and is the design's own: --t-ground inside a --t-bar panel steps *up* in light, so the design's markup puts the lightest rung in the ladder on a panel two rungs below it. Fixing that is an upstream decision about which surface a quoted payload takes, and this entry retires when it is made.

contradictions.design_says: HANDOFF.md:262 — the inline diff carries 'a 5-cell right-aligned line number', which reads as the number ending at cell 7 when measured from the 3-cell margin.
contradictions.design_also_says: The frame's own markup is `flex: 0 0 45px; text-align: right; padding-right: 9px` — a 5-cell field holding a 4-cell number and one cell of separation, so the number right-aligns to cell 6 and cell 7 is the separation. Restated at crates/tui/src/ui/diff.rs:209-212.
contradictions.app_follows: The markup. This is the single most re-raised finding in the project's history — judges have reported it across four separate runs, each reading the prose and none reading the 45px. Kept here so the fifth does not.

contradictions.design_says: HANDOFF.md's screen sections name raw ramp rungs: :274 puts the permission panel's sentence in 'neutral-300', :279 the option number in 'accent-300 on the selected row and neutral-600 on the rest'.
contradictions.design_also_says: The same document's own token table says agent prose is `--t-body` #e3dfeb = neutral-200 (HANDOFF.md:88), and semantic.css exposes no --tui-* role resolving to neutral-600 at all — palette.css:45 defines the step, nothing points at it. The screen prose predates the token layer the rest of the system was rebuilt onto.
contradictions.app_follows: The token layer, because it is the only one it can draw through. Two stage 5 judges reached opposite conclusions on the same frames from the same prose — one called the mapping correct 'through HANDOFF's superseded Nocturne table', the other called it a major deviation — which is the signature of a reference that says two things. What this wants upstream is the screen prose rewritten in semantic roles like the rest of the handoff.

contradictions.design_says: HANDOFF.md:395-396 — the empty state's third fact is `access`, and its value is the tier word; the design's own 1c/`14c` step offers `ask` / `read` / `write` / `all`.
contradictions.design_also_says: The design never says what the fact reads once the stored grants match no tier, which is the ordinary state rather than the edge: `permissions.yaml` gains a grant every time a permission prompt is answered with a lasting allow, and it is a plain file a developer edits. ADR 0001 §5 has already removed one of the four points (`write`) as a state that does not exist, and ADR 0001 puts `edit` outside the permissions model entirely, so `edit:` is ungrantable at every tier and distinguishes none of them.
contradictions.app_follows: The three stored per-tool states (`read:` / `shell:` / `edit:`) — what this directory actually permits — rather than a tier word that is only true until the file drifts. `transcript.rs`'s own note: a tier is what first run *writes*, not what is stored, and reporting one would be a guess printed as a fact on the screen whose whole job is to say what this directory permits. Deferred deliberately: the permissions model is being reworked and this fact's shape is settled with it. Retire this entry then — it is the one entry here whose retirement condition is an app change rather than a design fix.
